hunt.justification: CVE-2026-97229 is a critical CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE. This hunt provides the necessary business assurance that the critical integer overflow has not been triggered on the self-managed GitLab estate.

meta.analysis: A single rule on shell spawns by the git user is prone to false positives from legitimate hooks. This hunt correlates software version, delivery patterns, and execution prevalence using a phased approach and AI triage to reduce noise and provide a high-confidence verdict.

scenario.summary: An attacker exploits an integer overflow in GitLab's CI/CD regular expression compiler (CVE-2026-97229) by committing a malicious configuration file and a repository path containing UTF-8 characters to a public project. This triggers a control-flow hijack in the Onigmo regex engine when evaluating the crafted expression, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution as the 'git' user on unpatched self-managed instances.

meta.rationale: Focus exclusively on self-managed GitLab Community and Enterprise editions. GitLab.com is out of scope.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker exploited CVE-2026-97229 by planting a malicious .gitlab-ci.yml in a repository, causing an integer overflow in the Ruby Onigmo engine that executes arbitrary commands as the git user.

hunt.name: GitLab CI/CD Regex Compiler RCE Detection
hunt.description: This hunt covers the entire lifecycle of CVE-2026-97229 exploitation on self-managed GitLab instances. It begins by scoping the estate to vulnerable 19.2, 19.3, and 19.4 version branches. The hunt then moves through a phased flow: first identifying delivery evidence via configuration file writes and suspicious web activity, followed by a search for the successful execution phase where the GitLab worker process spawns rare shell or utility processes under the git account. An agent weighs the delivery and execution evidence together per host to provide a final verdict.

nodes.label: Rare processes spawned by GitLab workers

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_cmd_line) AS cmd, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(user_name) = LOWER('{{git_user}}') AND (LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%ruby%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%sidekiq%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%bundle%') AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/sh' OR LOWER(process_name) = 'sh' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/bash' OR LOWER(process_name) = 'bash' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/python%' OR LOWER(process_name) = 'python' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/curl' OR LOWER(process_name) = 'curl' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%/wget' OR LOWER(process_name) = 'wget') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY cmd HAVING host_count <= 3
config.description: Identify successful RCE by stack-counting rare shell and utility processes spawned by the Ruby application workers.
config.expected_signal: A rare shell command or network utility spawned by a GitLab worker is a high-fidelity indicator of successful RCE. Silence proves the absence of this specific behavior on the GitLab hosts during the window.
